SUBJECT: Mr. C. V. Starr - American.

It is learned that Mr C. V. Starr, American, arrived in Shanghai in 1921 and from then until his departure, was engaged chiefly in Insurance and Newspaper business. Mr Starr and his wife left Shanghai in September 1940, and are believed to be at present living in the United States of America.

Mr Starr was, prior to his departure, residing at 244 Hungjao Road, and was then a director of the American Asiatic Underwriters, and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Asia Life Insurance Company, these being American Insurance concerns and located at 17 The Bund. He was also President of the Board of Directors of the Post Mercury Co., 19 Avenue Edward VII, and proprietor of the foreign language newspaper, "The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury" and the Chinese edition of the same newspaper, the "Ta Mei Wan Pao", which newspapers were taken over by him in 1927. From 1937 until towards the end of 1941, these newspapers were considered to be pro-Chiang Kai-shek.

In July 1940, Fu Siau-en, Mayor of Greater Shanghai, was, it is believed, requested by Wang Ching-wei to arrange for the expulsion of Mr Starr together with six other foreign newspaper men from Shanghai. The reason for this was given as being due to the pro-Chungking attitude of their respective newspapers and other publications. In August 1940, Mr Starr received warning from the French Police that they had received information that an attempt may be made on his life by terrorists. As far as is known, no such attempt was

主题：C. V. Starr 先生 - 美国人。

据悉，美国人 C. V. Starr 先生于 1921 年抵达上海，从那时起直至其离开，主要从事保险和报业工作。Starr 先生及其妻子于 1940 年 9 月离开上海，据信目前居住在美国。

在离开之前，Starr 先生居住在虹桥路 244 号，当时他是美亚保险公司（American Asiatic Underwriters）的董事，以及亚洲人寿保险公司（Asia Life Insurance Company）的董事会主席，这两家均为位于外滩 17 号的美国保险公司。他还是位于爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）19 号的《文汇报》公司（Post Mercury Co.）的董事会主席，也是英文报纸《上海晚邮报与文汇报》（The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）及其中文版《大美晚报》的所有者，这些报纸是他于 1927 年接手的。从 1937 年到 1941 年底，这些报纸被认为持亲蒋介石立场。

1940 年 7 月，据信汪精卫要求大上海市长傅筱庵安排将 Starr 先生连同其他六名外国报人驱逐出上海。给出的理由是他们的报纸及其他出版物持亲重庆态度。1940 年 8 月，Starr 先生收到法国警察局的警告，称他们收到情报，恐怖分子可能企图暗杀他。据所知，并未发生此类企图

FURTHER TO : RE INFORMATION RECEIVED BY MR. STARR,C.V. FROM FRENCH
POLICE REGARDING THREATS TO HIS LIFE.

D.S.I. Konovaloff D. I. Glover.

Sir,

At 3.20 p.m. on the 23.8.40 Supt. Emelianoff
was interviewed by the undersigned re the information
as noted in the first report.

According to Supt. Emelianoff this information
had been obtained by the French Intelligence Service
and passed to him by Commander Fabre with the instructions
to inform the persons concerned accordingly. However,
on the morning of the 23.8.40 a further information was
passed by the French Intelligence Service to the French
Police to the effect that Mr. J. B. Powell, Editor of
Shanghai Weekly Review, is the only foreigner against
whom violence is to be used. It appears that the
terrorists intend to kidnap or assassinate Powell not
for political reasons but because he, is alleged, to be
a leader of a gang of saboteurs who have been operating
in North China. Mr. Powell, according to the information,
was implicated as a leader by a male Chinese, member of
a Sabotage gang, who, it is said, was apprehended by
the Dairen Gendarmerie at an unknown address on Yu Ya
Ching Road, Shanghai, sometime in June 1940.

It is worthy of note that assistance was recently
requested by the Japanese Gendarmerie to arrest a foreigner
named A. Powell, alias Milev, wanted as a leader of a
sabotage gang. For details please see the attached report

C.l.Misc. No. 143/40.

关于：Starr, C.V. 先生从法国警察局收到的有关对其生命威胁的情报。

副督察长 Konovaloff 督察 Glover。

先生，

1940年8月23日下午3时20分，签署人就第一份报告中 noted 的情报采访了 Emelianoff 警司。

据 Emelianoff 警司称，该情报是由法国情报部门获得，并由 Fabre 指挥官转交给他，指示他相应地通知相关人员。然而，1940年8月23日上午，法国情报部门向法国警察局传递了进一步的情报，大意是《密勒氏评论报》（Shanghai Weekly Review）编辑 J. B. Powell 先生是唯一将遭受暴力对待的外国人。看来，恐怖分子意图绑架或暗杀 Powell 并非出于政治原因，而是因为他据称是一个在华北活动的破坏团伙的头目。根据该情报，Powell 先生被一名中国男子指认为头目，该男子是破坏团伙的成员，据说于 1940 年 6 月的某个时候在上海虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）的一个不明地址被大连宪兵队逮捕。

值得注意的是，日本宪兵队最近请求协助逮捕一名名为 A. Powell、别名 Milev 的外国人，此人作为破坏团伙的头目被通缉。详情见附件报告

C.l.Misc. No. 143/40。

RE INFORMATION RECEIVED BY MR. STARR, C.V. FROM FRENCH POLICE
REGARDING THREATS TO HIS LIFE.

D.S.I. Konovaloff D. I. Glover.

（批：D.L. (Lime) I wonder if Mr. Starr or Mr. Gould would be interested in the services of General Kosich-Simonov - Chaffee. Please see attached letter.）
（批：Dels 13 R.W.Y. I do not think there is any ground for alarm at present / S.）
（印：RECEIVED 23 AUG 1940 CONSULAT GENERAL DE FRANCE A SHANGHAI）
（批：File. 23/8/40）

Sir,

Acting on instructions of Officer i/c C.l., D.I. Glover, the undersigned interviewed Mr. Starr, C.V., Managing Director of Asia Life Insurance Co., 17 the Bund and Post-Mercury Co., 19 Avenue Edward VII, at 3 p.m. the 22.8.40.

Mr. Starr, at his office, 17 The Bund, has divulged the following information which was passed to him personally by Super. EMELIANOFF of the French Police, Political Branch, on the 22.8.40 A.M.

"That the French Police have recently received information from very reliable sources (not disclosed) to the effect that certain elements engaged in terrorist activities in Shanghai, have received instructions to carry out several assassinations, and that the would-be victims are several foreigners amongst whom Mr. Starr and Mr. Randall Gould, Editor of Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury, are listed as the persons to be killed or kidnapped. Super. Emelianoff has emphasized the fact that this information had been received from such reliable sources that it should be treated without reserve and advised Mr. Starr to take adequate precautions in his movements, adding that Mr. R. Gould was informed of the information received and had also been advised to take precautions for his personal safety".

Mr. Starr expressed his opinion that taking into consideration the recent assassinations of two editors of the Post-Mercury Co., i.e. Mr. S. T. Chang and Mr. C. T. Chen, which acts have not changed the attitude and course of the Post-Mercury editorials, it is possible that the terrorists might

关于：Starr, C.V. 先生从法国警察局收到的有关对其生命威胁的情报。

副督察长 Konovaloff 督察 Glover。

（批：D.L. (Lime) 我想知道 Starr 先生或 Gould 先生是否会对 Kosich-Simonov - Chaffee 将军的服务感兴趣。请参见附信。）

（印：1940年8月23日收 法国驻上海总领事馆）
（批：归档。1940年8月23日）

先生，

按照刑事科主管警官、督察 Glover 的指示，签署人于 1940年8月22日下午3时采访了亚洲人寿保险公司（17 外滩）和《文汇报》公司（爱多亚路 19 号）总经理 C.V. Starr 先生。

Starr 先生在其位于外滩 17 号的办公室透露了以下信息，该信息是法国警察局政治处 Emelianoff 警司于 1940年8月22日上午亲自传递给他的。

“法国警察局最近从非常可靠的来源（未披露）收到情报，大意是在上海从事恐怖活动的某些分子已接到指令执行几起暗杀行动，预定受害者包括几名外国人，其中 Starr 先生和《上海晚邮报与文汇报》编辑 Randall Gould 先生被列为将被杀害或绑架的人员。Emelianoff 警司强调，该情报来自如此可靠的来源，以至于应毫无保留地予以重视，并建议 Starr 先生在行动中采取充分的预防措施，他还补充说，R. Gould 先生已获知所收到的情报，并也被建议为其人身安全采取预防措施”。

Starr 先生表达了他的观点，考虑到《文汇报》公司两名编辑即 S. T. Chang 先生和 C. T. Chen 先生最近遭暗杀，而这些行为并未改变《文汇报》社论的态度和方针，恐怖分子可能会

resolve to more effective means to attain their purpose.
Mr. Starr has also expressed his desire that the
S.M.Police would endeavour to establish the authenticity
of this information.
Upon being advised by the undersigned to take some
precautionary measures for his personal safety, Mr. Starr
stated that he would use a Russian Police Watchman (armed)
employed by the American Asiatic Underwriters, 17 The Bund,
as his bodyguard for the time being.
Super. Koulianoff will be interviewed re this in-
formation on the 23.8.40.

Starr 先生还表达了希望上海公共租界警务处努力核实该情报真实性的愿望。
当签署人建议他采取一些预防措施以保障其人身安全时，Starr 先生表示，他将暂时雇用一名由美亚保险公司（17 外滩）雇佣的俄罗斯警察看守（武装）作为他的保镖。
将于 1940年8月23日就此事采访 Koulianoff 警司。
